transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Lately I’ve been overwhelmed by guilt about letting everyone down at home and at work, even when people tell me it’s not that bad. I just feel like I'm failing the people who depend on me, and I can't seem to shake this feeling.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of guilt and failure, and have they been constant or have they come and gone over time?

This current low stretch has been dragging on for about five months now. Looking back, these cycles of sinking into these low, drained feelings alternating with periods of being overly revved up have been happening on and off for at least a few years, though they've gotten much worse over the past year.
Can you describe one of these periods when you felt 'overly revved up' - what were you experiencing and how did you behave during that time?

During those weeks, I feel an intense surge of energy where my thoughts race, I sleep only about four hours a night but wake up wired, and I talk so fast my coworkers can't get a word in. I get overly confident and take on tons of extra projects and events, thinking I'm the only one who can handle everything. I also get really touchy and easily snap at my family, even though I feel unusually upbeat.
Can you estimate how often these periods of feeling 'overly revved up' occur in a year, and do they significantly interfere with your daily life or relationships?

These cycles have happened a few times a year for at least several years, but they've become much more disruptive over this past year. They absolutely interfere with my life; my team at work has had to quietly pick up my slack when I fall behind, and my daughter recently told me she never knows which version of me she's coming home to.

Can you tell me more about how your mood shifts from the low, guilty feelings to the high, overly confident feelings - is it usually triggered by something specific or does it seem to happen on its own?

Usually, these cycles have just come and gone on their own over the years. But this most recent shift felt very tied to specific events: the high phase kicked off around a successful hospitality program rollout at work, and I crashed into this low, guilty state as that energy tapered off and family tensions with my husband and daughter intensified.
Can you clarify if your periods of feeling 'overly revved up' typically last for a few days, a week or two, or sometimes longer, and are they always followed by a crash into a low mood?

Those high-energy periods typically last for several weeks before I inevitably crash. Once that energy fades, I sink into a low, drained mood that lasts much longer, like this current stretch which has been going on for about five months now.
Can you confirm if your periods of feeling 'overly revved up' last at least 4 consecutive days, and do these episodes always transition into a depressive phase like the one you're experiencing now?

Yes, those revved-up periods definitely last much longer than four days, usually stretching on for a few weeks at a time. And yes, they always seem to end in a crash, transitioning right into a heavy, drained low like this current five-month slump that followed my work rollout.
Can you tell me if there are any periods where you feel completely normal, without either the high-energy or low, guilty feelings, and if so, how often these normal periods occur?
I'm not quite sure, and I haven't really thought about it. Lately, it feels like I am always either dealing with the highs or the lows, without much stable ground in between.

Can you help me understand if the duration and severity of your depressive episodes, like the current one, are typically proportional to the duration and intensity of the preceding high-energy episodes?

I'm not quite sure if they are directly proportional to each other. While I've noticed that the high-energy periods usually last a few weeks and the low periods drag on for months, I haven't tracked them closely enough to know if the intensity of one predicts how bad or long the other will be.
Do you experience any psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions, during either your high-energy or low, depressive episodes?

No, I have never experienced any hallucinations, delusions, or other psychotic symptoms during either my high-energy or low periods. Even when my thoughts are racing or I am feeling extremely down, I have always stayed grounded in reality.

Can you clarify if your high-energy periods, where you feel overly revved up, have ever led to significant problems in your relationships, work, or involved reckless behaviors that you later regretted?

I haven't engaged in any reckless behaviors, but those high-energy periods definitely strained my relationships at home and work. I would impulsively overcommit to too many projects, talk so fast in meetings that coworkers joked I wouldn't let them get a word in, and snap at my daughter over minor things. The constant shifting and irritability really took a toll on everyone around me.
During your high-energy periods, have you ever required hospitalization due to severe manic symptoms or posed a danger to yourself or others?
No, I've never been hospitalized during those high-energy periods. I have also never posed any danger to myself or to others when I felt that way.
Have you ever experienced any episodes of being 'overly revved up' that lasted less than 7 days, but were still significantly disruptive to your daily life or relationships?

Actually, those highly energized periods tend to last longer than just a week, usually stretching on for a few weeks at a time. During those weeks, my behavior is indeed quite disruptive to my daily life and relationships, which both my family and colleagues have definitely noticed.
Can you confirm if any of your high-energy periods have lasted less than 4 consecutive days but still caused significant disruption or impairment in your social or occupational functioning?
I'm not really sure about periods that short, as my high-energy phases typically last much longer. They usually go on for a few weeks at a time, so I haven't really experienced them being that brief.
Can you clarify if the significant disruption caused by your high-energy periods is primarily due to the duration of these episodes or the intensity of your behaviors during them?

It really feels like a combination of both. The intensity of my behavior during those weeks—like sleeping very little, talking too fast, and snapping at my family—creates immediate tension and makes my daughter feel like she doesn't know who she is coming home to. At the same time, because these phases last for several weeks, I have enough time to pile on way too many commitments, which eventually causes me to crash and leaves a trail of unfinished projects and strained relationships.

Can you estimate how many days your most recent 'overly revved up' period lasted before transitioning into this current low, guilty state, and did the severity of this low state seem to correlate with the intensity of the preceding high-energy episode?

My most recent high-energy period lasted for several weeks, probably about a month, before I transitioned into this low state. I'm not entirely sure if there is a direct correlation between the two, but this current low stretch has dragged on for about five months and feels incredibly heavy, especially coming off such an intense, active period.
Can you try to recall if the longer or more intense your high-energy periods are, the longer or more severe your subsequent low, depressive episodes tend to be?
I'm not quite sure if there is a direct connection like that. I haven't really tracked or compared the exact intensity or duration of the highs versus the lows in that much detail to know for sure.

Can you reflect on your past episodes and try to determine if there's any pattern where the severity or duration of your high-energy periods seems to predict the severity or duration of the following low, depressive episodes?

I'm really not sure and haven't thought about whether the intensity or duration of the highs predicts the lows. I just know the general pattern of having those high-energy periods for a few weeks followed by much longer, draining low periods. I don't know if they scale with each other at all.

Looking back at your past episodes, can you think of any instance where a particularly intense or long high-energy period was followed by a low, depressive episode that was unusually severe or long-lasting compared to your other episodes?

Yes, looking back, this current cycle is by far the most severe one I've experienced. After that high-energy period following my workplace program rollout, I crashed into this current low stretch, which has been dragging on for about five months now. It feels much more intense and heavy than any of the milder ups and downs I've had over the past few years.

Can you think of any instance where a less intense or shorter high-energy period was followed by a significantly shorter or less severe low, depressive episode, which might help clarify if there's a direct relationship between the two?
I’m not really sure about that. I haven't tracked my cycles closely enough in the past to notice if a shorter or less intense high-energy period was followed by a milder or shorter low period.

Can you think of any instance where you had a high-energy period that was shorter or less intense than usual, and if so, did the following low period seem to be shorter or less severe as well, which might help us understand the pattern of your episodes?

I'm not quite sure, as I haven't tracked my cycles closely enough to know if a shorter high-energy period leads to a shorter low period. I've really only noticed the general pattern of cycling between those highs and lows over the past few years. It is hard for me to pinpoint a specific connection like that.

Can you try to recall if there was ever a time when you had a high-energy period that was significantly shorter or less intense than your typical episodes, and if the following low period was also shorter or less severe, which could help clarify the relationship between the highs and lows?

I'm really not sure and haven't noticed a pattern of shorter or less intense cycles. I usually just recall my typical pattern of feeling highly revved up for a few weeks, followed by those long, heavy stretches of feeling low.

Can you think of any instance where the duration or severity of your low, depressive episodes seemed unrelated to the duration or severity of the preceding high-energy episodes, which might help us differentiate between possible diagnoses?

Yes, the durations of the high and low phases actually seem very different. While my high-energy periods typically only last for a few weeks, the low periods that follow are much longer and more drawn out. In fact, this current depressive stretch has already been dragging on for about five months.
Can you confirm whether the duration of your depressive episodes is always longer than the duration of your high-energy episodes, and if this pattern has been consistent throughout your experience?

Yes, that has been a very consistent pattern for me over the last few years. My high-energy phases usually only last for a few weeks, whereas the low, depressed periods drag on for much longer, like this current stretch which has already lasted for about five months.

Can you confirm if the pattern of having shorter high-energy episodes followed by longer depressive episodes has been consistent throughout your experience, without any instances where a short high-energy episode was followed by a similarly short or even longer depressive episode?

Yes, as far as I can remember, my pattern has consistently been short bursts of high energy lasting a few weeks followed by much longer, dragged-out low periods like this current five-month stretch. I don't recall ever having a low period that was short or brief after one of those high-energy phases—they always seem to turn into long, draining stretches.
Can you confirm if you have ever experienced a high-energy episode that lasted at least 7 days, but less than 2 weeks, and if so, how your behavior and functioning were during that time?

I've definitely had those high-energy episodes, though they typically last a bit longer—usually several weeks rather than under two weeks. During those phases, I feel unusually upbeat but touchy, sleep only about four hours a night without feeling tired, and take on way too many projects and events. My thoughts race and I talk so fast in meetings that my coworkers can't even get a word in.

Can you confirm if you have ever had a high-energy episode lasting less than 4 consecutive days, and if so, did it meet the full criteria for a hypomanic episode, including significant disruption in social or occupational functioning?

No, my high-energy episodes actually last much longer than four days, typically spanning several weeks where I feel extremely energized, barely sleep, and take on too many projects. While that behavior did cause some strain with my daughter and coworkers, my major struggles and drop-offs in functioning have been most severe during my low periods.

Can you confirm if there has ever been a time when you experienced a high-energy episode that lasted at least 7 days but was not followed by a major depressive episode, which could help differentiate between the possible diagnoses of bipolar I disorder and bipolar II disorder?

As far as I can remember, my high-energy periods—which usually last for a few weeks—have always been followed by a crash into a low, drained phase. I don't recall ever having one of those high-energy stretches that didn't eventually lead into a depressive period.

Can you confirm if you have ever experienced a high-energy episode that lasted at least 7 days and caused significant impairment in social or occupational functioning, but did not meet the full criteria for a manic episode?

Yes, my high-energy periods definitely last for several weeks, which is well over 7 days. During those times, I feel unusually upbeat, sleep very little, and take on way too many projects, which certainly causes some strain and chaotic situations with my family and coworkers. However, I have never lost complete control or needed to be hospitalized, even though it is a very noticeable and disruptive departure from my normal self.
Can you confirm whether you have ever experienced a manic episode that lasted at least 7 days, or if all your high-energy episodes have been shorter and less severe, lasting only a few days?

My high-energy periods actually last for a few weeks rather than just a few days, but they have never been so severe that I lost control or needed to be hospitalized. While they make me very active, talkative, and sleep-deprived, they are more about overcommitting and acting differently than usual rather than a full manic episode.
